stem: Make $x$ the subject of the formula ${=a}x - py = {=b}x + qy$.
solution: Collect the terms containing $x$ on the left and the other terms on the right: ${=a}x - {=b}x = py + qy$.
Take out the common factor on each side: $x({=a} - {=b}) = y(p + q)$.
Simplify the bracket on the left: ${=k}x = y(p + q)$.
notes: The subject x appears in a term on each side, so the student must first collect the x-terms on one side (the book's method in we16: isolate, collect, factorise, divide) and only then take x out as the common factor. Parameters: b in 2..8 and a = b + 2 .. b + 6, so a - b = k is always 2..6: never 0 (no division by zero), never 1 (no '1x'), never negative. The right-hand side p y + q y factorises to y(p + q), so both sides are factorised before dividing by the number k. Letters p, q, y are fixed; only a and b change (about 35 distinct stems). The answer (p + q)y/k is a single expression, so any equivalent arrangement is acceptable. No mcq, so no distractors.
